title: Traversing an Array
objectives: Walk through an array from start to end with a loop
Use the size of the array as the loop limit

hook.text: Will you write out EVERY element of an array one by one as "array[0]", "array[1]", "array[2]"...? Now you know loops. It is time to combine them.

concept.heading: Loop + index = traversal
concept.body: To walk through an array, you use a FOR loop that takes the index variable from 0 up to the last index of the array: FOR i ← 0 TO (size - 1) STEP 1. In each round, array[i] reaches that round's element.

concept.heading: The size sets the limit
concept.body: In an array of N elements, the loop should run from i = 0 to i = N - 1. If you go all the way to i = N (one too many), you get an out-of-bounds error. This is the most common mistake when working with arrays: the "fencepost" error.

workedExamples.prompt: Print all the elements of an array in order.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
numbers ← [10, 20, 30]
FOR i ← 0 TO 2 STEP 1
  WRITE numbers[i]
END_LOOP

steps.explain: An array with 3 elements is created.
i runs from 0 to 2 (3 elements, indexes 0-2).
In each round numbers[i] is written: 10, 20, 30.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: An array with 4 elements, with indexes from 0 to 3.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
Which loop limit walks through an array of 6 elements exactly?

feedback.correct: Correct. In an array of 6 elements, the valid indexes go from 0 to 5.
feedback.incorrect: In an array of 6 elements, the last valid index is 5 (6 - 1); the loop should run from 0 to 5.

exercises.question: What happens if you walk through an array of 6 elements with "FOR i ← 0 TO 6 STEP 1"?
options: In the last round, array[6] gives an out-of-bounds error

feedback.correct: Correct. When i = 6, array[6] is not valid (the last index is 5): an out-of-bounds error.
feedback.incorrect: When i goes up to 6, the code tries to reach array[6], which is outside the valid range (0-5).

exercises.question: Put the steps of the algorithm that prints all the elements of an array in the correct order (an array of 3 elements).
Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: When walking through an array with a loop, the loop limit should be one less than the ___ of the array.

summary: To walk through an array, use a loop that runs from i = 0 to size - 1.
In an array of N elements, the valid indexes go from 0 to N - 1.
Setting the loop limit wrong (the fencepost error) is the most common array mistake.
